contexts.text: What notion they have conceived of Heaven...
(Being in worldly and corporeal affections, man) can have notions concerning celestial and spiritual ones.
General notions must precede...
In order that some notion may be had of this Thing...
Those things fall into the shade (of the understanding) which do not coincide with the things of which it before had some notion.
(Spirits) have thought from states of life, and this without notion of times.
Hence no notion of time enters their thoughts; but a notion of state and its progressions. Notions are taken from those things which are and come forth before the senses.
The Intellectual of the Church is the understanding with the men of the Church concerning truths and goods... thus their notion, concept, or idea, concerning them.
Nevertheless the Angels have no notion and idea of time and space... HH 191. HH 195.
As the idea concerning God, with all notion of Him, has been torn to pieces...
Even general notions (of this science) would All innumerable sheets.
Those things which are of life... are successively inserted into this general notion.
For each notion contains infinite things...
The notion of this has been sometimes given me in sleep.

Therefore the notion of time and space does not exist with Spirits, except with those who are corporeal... and even with them there is no reflection upon such things, and without reflection there is no notion of such things; as may be evident from man in the body: when he is not reflecting upon such, and corporeal, things, neither is he then in the notion of them.
As they (then) have no other notion than that of time... they deduce absurdities...

I have been led into a certain perception of forms, the notion of which far surpasses... the notions taken from geometrical things; for the forms... so surpass the forms of geometrical notions, that they cannot possibly be perceived from them. SE 3484.
Concerning the notion of love and of heaven.
An idea or notion of it occurred exceedingly gross, which ideas and notions can scarcely be described... But when the persuasive life of Spirits occurred, the idea or notion was subtle...
That he should have the notion (of the spirit) which he has now, had been impossible...
As the Sun is not such as it is in the world, they can have no notion of time; but only of state...
How that natural thought, and especially sensuous thought, cannot recede from the notion of space and time.
Still, they have a notion of heat and cold, and also of light and shade; but not from time; but from the state of their life.
From this general notion concerning the contents, it may be seen...
